title: 3D epigenome of glial cell types in developing human cortex.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Europe PMC record: subscription only, no PMCID, hasSuppl=N, no database cross-references, only one text-mined accession (rs4449074, a SNP ID, not a dataset). NCBI elink from PubMed 42686907 returns no GEO, SRA or BioProject links. Three GEO DataSets searches (outer radial glia + PLAC-seq, microglia + OPC + PLAC-seq) returned 0 hits. The Nature article page redirects to a login. The same lab's 2020 companion dataset in NeMO (Neuroscience Multi-omic Archive, nemo:dat-uioqy8b) is marked Restricted: 263 files, about 2.6 TB.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: From the abstract and a search snippet only: four glial types (vRG, ventricular radial glia; oRG, outer radial glia; OPC, oligodendrocyte precursor cells; microglia). Radial glia came from 6 donors at gestational weeks 15–18; microglia and OPCs from 9 donors at weeks 22–24. Assays were RNA, chromatin accessibility, DNA methylation and 3D chromatin contacts. cCREs (candidate regulatory elements) were tested in transgenic mice; 112 schizophrenia variants were prioritised by ML. No deposit location or supplement contents were seen.

a1_downloadable.note: No open deposit found. There are no GEO, SRA or Zenodo links, the paper and supplement are paywalled and not in PMC, and the lab's matching 2020 dataset in NeMO is controlled access (needs an access application). Checked via API and search, not the paper's data statement, which was not retrievable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not checked; no files seen. The likely labels (cell-type-specific cCRE calls, enhancer-gene loops) are the authors' analysis outputs. Only the transgenic-mouse enhancer results would be a measured label, and those are probably a small supplementary list.

a5_enough_rows.note: Unknown. The measured label (in vivo enhancer tests) is likely tens of elements, not thousands.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; the 2020 companion raw deposit is about 2.6 TB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Processed peak and loop files would fit on a laptop, but none were found.

a8_label_provenance.note: Cell-type-specific cCRE labels are computed from the same accessibility and contact data that would serve as features, so they are circular. Only the mouse transgenic results trace back to a physical measurement.

backbone.name: AlphaGenome or DNABERT-2 (DNA sequence models) would fit cCRE sequences
backbone.hardware: CPU for small sets of elements

integration.partner_dataset: VISTA Enhancer Browser (in vivo mouse enhancer tests)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do glia-specific open chromatin and 3D contacts predict which human elements drive glial expression in vivo better than sequence alone?

controls.external_validation: VISTA transgenic enhancer results would be the obvious external set

honest_claim_h3: Not stateable without the files. At best: predicts glial cCRE activity among elements already selected as accessible in sorted mid-gestation cells from 6–9 donors.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence plus glial chromatin openness and 3D contacts to predict which regulatory elements switch genes on in developing brain glia.
plain_idea.train_on: Candidate regulatory regions from four sorted glial cell types, each with its sequence, accessibility, methylation and contact features. Number of examples unknown; no files were accessible.
plain_idea.predict: Whether an element is active in a cell type, measured by the authors' transgenic mouse embryo enhancer assays, which are probably few.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups mapping schizophrenia risk variants to glial enhancers could rank variants for lab tests. Here, though, the data cannot be obtained without a controlled-access application.

label_elsewhere.sources: VISTA Enhancer Browser (known resource) holds in vivo enhancer test results, but few are glia-specific.
label_elsewhere.why: VISTA could supply external enhancer-activity labels, but the glial-specific features from this paper are not openly available.

ml_idea: Predict in vivo glial enhancer activity from sequence plus cell-type chromatin features. Blocked: there is no open data, and the cCRE labels are derived from the features.

effort.compute_note: Not estimable; no files were accessible.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find the paper's data availability statement. If processed peaks and loops are only in NeMO restricted access, which is the likely case given the 2020 companion, the project is dead.

verdict_reason: A1 fails: no open data found. The paper is paywalled with no supplement in Europe PMC, has no GEO, SRA or Zenodo links, and the same lab's companion dataset sits in NeMO restricted access. The available labels (cCRE calls) are also derived from the features, and the measured mouse enhancer tests are likely too few.
